__doc: Floors of the heavy review (evals/heavy-recall), per case set and model, read by evals/investigation/gate.js through run-recall.js --targets. Same rules as the finder's (evals/investigation/targets.json): two runs of one review code, the per-PR run-to-run recall difference, sigma = sdPerPrRunDiff / sqrt(2) / sqrt(15) * sqrt(1.5) for a two-run baseline, recallFloor = mean - 2.2 sigma rounded down, collapse floors at about half the observed findings and tool calls, under the judge below.
Runs, judgments and the scripts that computed these floors: kodustech/kodus-eval-runs, runs/2026-11-02_heavy-calibration.
RATCHET: a PR that moves a heavy review's recall on purpose recalibrates here, with two runs as evidence.

deepseek-v4-flash@fireworks, calibrated 2026-11-02 from 2 local runs (runs 1 and 2 on 7516dc055), judge gpt-5.6-luna low: recall 0.564 and 0.492 (15 PRs paired), mean 0.528, sdPerPrRunDiff 0.255, sigma 0.057. recallFloor = mean - 2.2 sigma = 0.4. Collapse floors at about half the observed means: 4.73 findings and 39.5 tool calls per PR.

Collapse floors at about half the observed means: 7.17 findings and 57.6 tool calls per PR.

Deliberate break, 2026-11-02 (local, deepseek-v4-flash@fireworks, controlled): the lenses run and their findings are dropped (runHeavyLensPasses): recall 0.460 on 13 PRs (2 not measured, provider error), above the 0.40 floor. DeepSeek's run-to-run noise puts its floor 13 points under its mean, so losing the lenses (about 7 points) does not trip the weekly; the experiment (evals/experiment.js, step heavy) compares a change PR by PR and is what catches a drop that size.
